---
title: "About me"
---

I'm a health economist at the Centre for Health Economics and Medicines
Evaluation (CHEME), Bangor University, where I have been a **Research Fellow in
Pharmacoeconomics** since 2023. Before that I was a Research Officer at CHEME,
first in Pharmacoepidemiology and then in Health Technology Assessment.

Most of my work is economic evaluation run alongside clinical trials, such as
the CASTLE and EXPO trials, together with methods work on problems that
health technology assessment keeps running into, such as extrapolating survival
beyond the end of a trial.

## Background

I came to health economics through psychology and applied statistics. I hold a
**PhD in Sport and Exercise Psychology** from Bangor University, where I used
quantitative and machine-learning methods to study the training pathways for
outdoor leadership qualifications. Before that I read **Geography** (BSc, First
Class) at Bangor, with a final-year project on individual decision-making in
Scottish avalanche terrain.

That route left me with a broad statistical toolkit, including Bayesian and
frequentist modelling, structural equation and multilevel models, and machine
learning, and with a habit of explaining results to people who are not
statisticians.

Alongside my university post I have also carried out independent research
consulting; it is listed on my [CV](academic_cv.qmd).

## Beyond research

Since 2014 I have been a member of **Llanberis Mountain Rescue Team**, serving
as a team member, welfare officer, committee member and vice chair.

From 2019 to 2022 I also worked part-time for **Outreach Rescue** as a
specialist rescue operative and instructor, training emergency-service
personnel in rope and swift-water rescue to national standards. During the
COVID-19 pandemic this included working as a helicopter medic, repatriating
North Sea oil and gas workers.
